samples.summary: New `isEmptyStoredColor` dereferences a null `StoredColor`, crashing the render path on attacker-controlled slide JSON (stored DoS)
samples.evidence: `isEmptyStoredColor` guards only `c === undefined` (line 60), then falls through to `c.kind === 'srgb' && c.value.trim()` (line 62). A JSON `null` therefore takes `typeof c === 'object'` and throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null`. Before this change every caller went through `defaultColorResolver`, whose first line is `if (c == null) return undefined` (line 15), and slides' `makeColorResolver` likewise starts `if (c == null) return themeText` (packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:55) — so null was safe. The new helper is now on the paint hot path: paint-layout.ts:388/453/555, table-renderer.ts:464/573, and color.ts:182/187 (caret). Vector: a workspace member or API-key holder PUTs slides content whose element `data.blocks[].inlines[].style.color` is `null` (or `{kind:'srgb', value: 42}` — `c.value.trim()` throws the same way). `writeSlidesRoot` stores `root.slides = document.slides` verbatim (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:104) and `assertValidSlide`/`assertValidElement` only check id/type/frame/background (docs-content.controller.ts:376-435), while `migrateElement` passes textBody through untouched (packages/slides/src/model/migrate.ts:155-168). Every collaborator who opens the deck then throws inside `paintLayout` on each frame — a persistent denial of service on shared content.

samples.summary: PPTX `<a:pPr lvl>` still raw-interpolates untrusted `block.listLevel` in the same function whose color children were just hardened
samples.evidence: `const lvl = block.listLevel ? ` lvl="${block.listLevel}"` : '';` interpolates the model value with no numeric coercion or closed lookup, into `<a:pPr algn="${algn}"${lvl}...>` (line 114). Unlike docs blocks (whose Yorkie Tree attributes are re-read with `Number(attrs.listLevel)` — frontend yorkie-doc-store.ts:459, backend docs-tree.ts:414), slides text bodies are plain JSON persisted verbatim by `writeSlidesRoot` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:104) with no per-block validation in `assertValidElement` (docs-content.controller.ts:415-435). Same defect class as the `<w:jc>` case this change fixed; `<a:alpha val="${c.alpha}"/>` and the lumMod/tint/shade siblings in packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:25-29 interpolate model values raw for the same reason.

samples.summary: `toRgbHexColor` assumes a string and throws on a non-string `StoredColor.value` handed to it by the PPTX exporter
samples.evidence: Line 104 calls `color.trim()` after only a truthiness check. `storedColorToThemeColor` passes `c.value` straight in (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:188) and `InlineStyle.color` is `StoredColor`, whose `srgb` arm carries whatever JSON was stored — slides element JSON is persisted verbatim (backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:104), so `{kind:'srgb', value: 42}` or `{kind:'srgb', value: {}}` is storable. The export then throws instead of failing closed to `undefined`, converting a poisoned deck into a permanent export failure for every user of that deck. A `typeof color !== 'string'` guard at the top of the normalizer makes the fail-closed contract the doc claims actually total.

samples.summary: The "closed lookup" `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS[style.alignment]` resolves prototype-chain keys, so it is not actually closed
samples.evidence: `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` is a plain object literal, so `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS['toString']`, `['constructor']`, `['valueOf']`, `['__proto__']` all return inherited values rather than `undefined`; `?? 'left'` never fires and line 143 emits e.g. `<w:jc w:val="function toString() { [native code] }"/>`. The inherited values contain no `"` or `<`, so this is not an escape from the attribute, but it defeats the stated "can only ever carry an ST_Jc token" guarantee and produces schema-invalid OOXML from a value an attacker chooses (`alignment: 'toString'` passes the new backend check only on non-docs paths, but the CRDT is writable directly over Yorkie). Same pattern at packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:79 (`ALGN[...] ?? 'l'`) and :268 (`UNDERLINE_STYLE_TO_U[...] ?? 'sng'`). Use `Object.create(null)`, a `Map`, or `Object.hasOwn` before the lookup.

samples.summary: The new `assertValidBlockStyle` gate covers only the docs arm and only `alignment`; identical blocks enter the same CRDT unvalidated through the slides arm and direct Yorkie writes
samples.evidence: The added guard runs from `assertValidDocsBody` → `assertValidBlock` (line 295) only. The slides arm of the *same* PUT handler (`assertValidSlidesBody`, lines 343-435) validates only `meta`, the four top-level arrays, and each element's `id`/`type`/`frame` — the docs `Block[]` inside `element.data.blocks`/`textBody` is written verbatim by `writeSlidesRoot` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:104), so `alignment`, `listLevel`, `headingLevel`, `color` and friends reach the CRDT and the PPTX/DOCX exporters unchecked. The docs Yorkie document is also writable directly over the collaborative websocket, which never passes through this controller. The header comment's claim that rejecting here "keeps the garbage out of the document in the first place" therefore holds for one writer out of several — the sinks remain the only real defense, which argues for hardening every sink (see the `lvl`/`alpha` finding) rather than relying on this gate.
searchedFor: grep 'migrateElement' across packages (only slides/src/model/migrate.ts, textBody untouched)
grep 'listLevel'/'headingLevel' across packages/**/src (coercion only in docs-tree.ts and yorkie-doc-store.ts)

samples.summary: `<w:pStyle w:val="Heading${headingLevel}"/>` interpolates the model value raw, unlike every other value-typed attribute in the change
samples.evidence: `buildParagraphPropertiesXml(block.style, block.type === 'heading' ? block.headingLevel : undefined)` reaches line 132 of docx-style-map.ts, which interpolates `headingLevel` with only a truthiness check. I could not complete an exploit chain: both deserializers coerce (`Number(attrs.headingLevel)` at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:453 and packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:409), so a hostile string becomes `NaN` and is skipped by the truthiness test, and the API validator does not check the field but the CRDT round-trip does the coercion. Hence low-to-medium confidence — but this is the one remaining value-typed attribute in the DOCX exporter not routed through a fail-closed converter, contrary to the rule the change's own design-doc table states, and it would become injectable the moment an export path is fed a Document that skips the Tree deserializer.

finding.summary: New `isEmptyStoredColor` dereferences an untrusted `StoredColor` without a type guard — a `null` color or an `{ kind: 'srgb', value: <non-string> }` persisted through the content PUT API throws a TypeError inside the paint path, crashing the renderer for every viewer of the document (stored DoS).
finding.evidence: `isEmptyStoredColor` (packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:59-63) does `if (c === undefined) return false;` then `typeof c === 'string' ? ... : c.kind === 'srgb' && c.value.trim() === ''`. For `c === null` (typeof 'object', not undefined) it evaluates `c.kind` → `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null`. For `{ kind: 'srgb', value: 42 }` it evaluates `(42).trim()` → `TypeError: c.value.trim is not a function`. Before this delta the same input was harmless: `resolve(c === '' ? undefined : c)` passed `null` straight to the resolver, and slides' `makeColorResolver` (packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:55) returns the theme text color for `c == null`, while `resolveColor` (packages/slides/src/model/theme.ts:102) returns a non-string `value` verbatim without throwing. Attack path: an authenticated caller (workspace member or API key) PUTs a slides body to `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:ws/documents/:id/content`; `assertValidSlidesBody`/`assertValidElement` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:415-435) validate only `id`/`type`/`frame`, and `writeSlidesRoot` assigns `root.slides = document.slides` verbatim (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:104), so `slides[i].elements[j].text.blocks[k].inlines[l].style.color = null` (or `{kind:'srgb',value:42}`) is persisted unchanged. Every client that renders the deck reaches `resolveStoredColor` from `paintLayout` (packages/docs/src/view/paint-layout.ts:388, 453, 555), `table-renderer.ts:464/573` and `resolveColorAtPosition` (color.ts:182) and throws, so the canvas render loop dies for all collaborators until the poisoned value is removed out-of-band. Fix: make the guard total (`typeof c !== 'object' || c === null` → false; `typeof c.value === 'string' && c.value.trim() === ''`).

mergedFrom.summary: DOCX attribute injection via `style.alignment`: the sibling sink in the very function this change hardened is still interpolated raw into `<w:jc w:val="..."/>`

finding.summary: `style.alignment` is interpolated unescaped and unvalidated into `<w:jc w:val="…">` — the same OOXML attribute-injection sink class this change hardens for colors, three lines below the fixed code
finding.evidence: buildParagraphPropertiesXml does `const align = style.alignment === 'justify' ? 'both' : style.alignment;` then `parts.push(`<w:jc w:val="${align}"/>`)` for anything that is not the literal 'left' (docx-style-map.ts:123-126). Unlike `fontFamily` (escaped at line 70-71) and now `color`/`backgroundColor` (normalized at 95/99), `align` gets neither escaping nor an allowlist. BlockStyle.alignment is typed as a closed union, but the runtime value comes from the Yorkie tree attributes with an unchecked cast: `partial.alignment = attrs.alignment as BlockStyle['alignment']` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:220), and `normalizeBlockStyle` only spreads defaults (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:272-274) — no validation anywhere on that path. Attack: a collaborator with write access to a shared doc (or anything writing the tree attr, incl. the backend docs-tree serializer) sets the block attribute `alignment` to `center"/><w:pStyle w:val="x` (or `a" w:x="`); when any other user exports the document, DocxExporter emits that string verbatim into word/document.xml (and header1.xml/footer1.xml via buildHeaderFooterXml), closing the `<w:jc>` element and injecting attacker-chosen OOXML into a file other users open in Word. Note the PPTX exporter does allowlist the same field (`ALGN[block.style.alignment] ?? 'l'`, packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:79), which is the pattern missing here. Confidence is medium only because I could not confirm the Yorkie server accepts an arbitrary `alignment` attribute value from a peer client; the exporter-side sink itself is unambiguous.

finding.summary: The docs content PUT API validates only the *shape* of `style`, not its values, so arbitrary strings persist into the CRDT and reach unescaped OOXML attribute sinks
finding.evidence:
`assertValidBlock` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:254-306) checks `id`, `type`, that `style` is an object, and array-ness of `inlines`/`tableData.rows`/`cells` — deliberately, per its own comment, "just the fields the writer unconditionally dereferences". No block-style or inline-style value is validated. `writeDocsRoot` then persists them verbatim (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:143, 174-184).

This is the enabling half of the `w:jc` injection above and is the reason that fixing only the color sinks leaves the class open: every current and future string-valued style field that an exporter interpolates is attacker-controlled. Surveyed the whole DOCX/PPTX attribute surface for other reachable string sinks — `fontFamily` is escaped (docx-style-map.ts:70-73, pptx text.ts:300), `headingLevel` is coerced with `Number()` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:438, docs-tree.ts:409) so at worst yields `Heading NaN`, `verticalAlign`/`borderStyle` are cast unchecked (yorkie-doc-store.ts:251,257) but the DOCX table writer emits no `vAlign`/`tcBorders` (docx-exporter.ts:301-323), `image.src` never enters XML (only the zip + an internally generated rId), and DOCX emits no hyperlinks at all — so `alignment` is the one live string sink today. Validating style values at the trust boundary (or per-sink allowlists) would make that robust rather than incidental.
